reasons: Claimed status is compliant and the rendered redline is identical to the original paragraphs with no comment attached, which is the expected output for a compliant finding — nothing is being raised against the counterparty.

The cited text meets the preferred position on every material term: 19.1 professional/workmanlike performance plus material conformance to documentation and specifications; 19.2 a ninety-day Deliverable conformance warranty running from the later of delivery or acceptance and Hosted Services conformance for the whole subscription term; 19.3 no intentionally introduced malicious code and Applicable Law compliance; 19.4 re-perform/repair/replace escalating to termination and refund of Fees paid.

The 19.5 disclaimer is limited to implied warranties and expressly does not limit any express warranty, service level, indemnity or remedy, so it does not swallow the express warranty and the 'AS IS' walk-away is not implicated.

The failed deterministic period check is a phrasing artifact only — the period is spelled out as 'ninety days' without a numeral — and does not indicate a substantive shortfall; the rationale correctly identifies this.

Minor housekeeping: the rationale refers to an 'attached edit' inserting '(90)' that does not appear in the rendered redline. Since no substantive change is warranted for a compliant clause, the unchanged redline is correct, but the rationale should drop the reference to a non-existent edit.
